expectations.text: Recognizes the brand-new-property case: the platform UI cannot be expected to show the conversion within the session, since events take hours to appear and a fresh conversion action starts in a waiting status
expectations.evidence: The transcript references the exception generically ('Miravelle does qualify for the skill's one named exception (brand-new property, no traffic yet...)') but then treats the empty Events Manager as 'one concrete anomaly ... that needs a root cause,' and marks check 5 as an outright 'FAIL, critical' requiring diagnosis (ad blocker, wrong Pixel ID, unpublished container) rather than explaining it as an expected hours-long delay or waiting status.

expectations.text: Issues a provisional PASS explicitly labelled as provisional - never a plain GO or 'verified'
expectations.evidence: The decision issued is 'DECISION: NO-GO (provisional PASS not yet earned - payload unverified, platform-UI check failed)' — no provisional PASS is actually issued, only withheld.

expectations.text: Conditions the provisional pass on debug-mode evidence plus a correct, inspected payload
expectations.evidence: "that provisional path still requires debug-mode evidence *plus* a correct payload — you have the first, not the second. So you're not even at 'provisional PASS' yet."

expectations.text: Mandates re-verification the moment the first live conversions land
expectations.evidence: "Once a real event lands in Events Manager with correct value, re-run the full sequence once more using an actual campaign click (after launch, in the first hours) to confirm the click identifier (fbclid) survives to the order."

expectations.text: Requires re-running the test conversion on the consent-reject path, not only the accept path
expectations.evidence: "Re-run the test purchase with consent **rejected**, confirm nothing fires." and "Reject-path test, not just accept (untested): you only tested consent-accept ... Test both paths before launch"

expectations.text: States the reject path is where tracking signal silently dies
expectations.evidence: The only reject-path concern raised is the opposite direction: "if the pixel fires on the reject path too, that's a compliance problem, not just a measurement one" — there is no statement that the reject path is where signal silently dies/is lost.

expectations.text: With consent-regulated traffic the majority of the audience, treats the consent path as a pre-launch fix rather than a risk-accepted deferral
expectations.evidence: The transcript notes 'France and Germany are both consent-regulated (CNIL / TTDSG)' and treats reject-path testing as a 'hard skill requirement, not optional polish,' but it never establishes that consent-regulated traffic is the majority of the audience.

expectations.text: Notes that changing what fires on the consent-reject path needs privacy or legal sign-off
expectations.evidence: No mention of privacy or legal sign-off anywhere in the transcript; the reject-path issue is framed only as a technical/compliance test to run, with no sign-off requirement noted.

expectations.text: Requires testing on the live published site outside preview mode, since a container can work in preview and never have been published
expectations.evidence: "Confirm the GTM container is actually published, not just previewed. This is the single most common cause of 'works in preview, nothing live' ... invisible until you specifically test the *live* site with preview mode closed."

expectations.text: Requires refreshing the confirmation page after the test purchase to check no second event fires
expectations.evidence: There is no mention anywhere in the transcript of refreshing the confirmation page to check for a duplicate/second event firing.

expectations.evidence: "confirm: event name = `Purchase`, value = the amount actually paid after the discount code (not the €12 list price) ... currency = EUR, an `event_id`, and `fbp`/`fbc` cookies present."

expectations.text: The test journey starts by landing with the click identifier in the URL, walking the exact path a paid click takes
expectations.evidence: The report explicitly excuses the missing click ID rather than requiring it: "no click ID (expected pre-launch, no ad click yet)" — the test procedure never requires starting the journey with a click identifier in the URL to mimic a paid click before launch.

expectations.text: Recognizes the brand-new-property case: the platform UI cannot be expected to show the conversion within the session, since events take hours to appear and a fresh conversion action starts in a waiting status
expectations.evidence: The transcript never frames the empty Events Manager as a normal delay for a brand-new pixel/property. No mention of processing lag or a 'waiting'/unverified pixel status for new properties.

expectations.text: Issues a provisional PASS explicitly labelled as provisional - never a plain GO or 'verified'
expectations.evidence: The transcript opens with 'No — don't mark it verified' and closes with 'is not "verified" — it's an open bug.' This is an outright rejection of the verification claim, not a provisional pass of any kind.

expectations.text: Conditions the provisional pass on debug-mode evidence plus a correct, inspected payload
expectations.evidence: No provisional pass is issued at all (see item 2), so there is no conditioning of a pass on debug-mode evidence plus payload inspection — instead the transcript demands a full re-test before any verdict is given.

expectations.text: Mandates re-verification the moment the first live conversions land
expectations.evidence: The transcript's checklist is entirely pre-launch ('Re-run the test per the checklist above ... and only call it done once...'); there is no instruction to re-verify once real/live conversions start flowing after launch.

expectations.text: Requires re-running the test conversion on the consent-reject path, not only the accept path
expectations.evidence: Consent is discussed only in terms of acceptance: '"I accepted the cookie banner" needs to translate into the CMP calling gtag(...)' and 'confirm analytics_storage/ad_storage/... actually flip to granted after accepting.' No instruction to test the reject/decline path.

expectations.text: States the reject path is where tracking signal silently dies
expectations.evidence: There is no discussion of the consent-reject path at all, let alone a claim that tracking silently dies there; the consent discussion is confined to the accept flow.

expectations.text: With consent-regulated traffic the majority of the audience, treats the consent path as a pre-launch fix rather than a risk-accepted deferral
expectations.evidence: The France/Germany GDPR point is used to justify deferred mitigation via server-side tracking ('plan to add Meta Conversions API (server-side) alongside the pixel — it's the standard mitigation...'), which is a deferral to a follow-up mitigation, not a mandate to fix the consent path itself before launch; and the reject path specifically is never addressed.

expectations.text: Notes that changing what fires on the consent-reject path needs privacy or legal sign-off
expectations.evidence: No mention of the reject path or of privacy/legal sign-off anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Requires testing on the live published site outside preview mode, since a container can work in preview and never have been published
expectations.evidence: The re-test instructions focus on browser/extension conditions ('Redo the test purchase in an incognito window with zero extensions') and consent/network checks, not on confirming the GTM container version was actually published live as opposed to merely passing in preview/debug mode.

expectations.text: Requires refreshing the confirmation page after the test purchase to check no second event fires
expectations.evidence: No mention anywhere of refreshing the confirmation/thank-you page to check for duplicate firing.
